name: qsv-timebucketp
description: Bucket time-series data into time windows (e.g. 15-minute, overlapping, or weekly from Monday) and aggregate them, optionally per group. Also computes rolling look-back windows (e.g. a trailing 2-hour average at each row) and can fill empty windows. Complements `sqlp`'s `DATE_TRUNC`, which only buckets by calendar unit.

args.name: input
args.description: The input CSV file. The file must have headers. If the file has a pschema.json file, it is used to type the columns unless --infer-len is set to a value other than the default. Stdin is not supported. A snappy-compressed (.sz) input is decompressed first, and an --output ending in .sz is snappy-compressed. Lines starting with QSV_COMMENT_CHAR are skipped. QSV_POLARS_FLOAT_PRECISION and QSV_OUTPUT_BOM apply to the output, as in sqlp and pivotp.

options.description:
Comma-separated aggregations, as func:column pairs, e.g. sum:sales,mean:temp. The functions are: first, last, sum, min, max, mean, median, quantile@

(alias q@

, p in [0, 1]), len. Each is output as _, e.g. sales_sum, or temp_quantile_0.95 for quantile@0.95. len takes no column: it counts the rows in each window and is output as "count".
Add _lower_boundary and _upper_boundary columns before the index column. Window mode only.
Also group by these columns (comma-separated). Windows are computed separately for each group.
Which window boundaries are inclusive: left, right, both or none. Defaults to left in window mode and to right in rolling mode.
The strptime format of a text --index column, e.g. %m/%d/%Y or "%d.%m.%Y %H:%M". Without time fields the index is read as dates, otherwise as datetimes.
Use comma as decimal separator when READING the input. Note that you will need to specify an alternate --delimiter.

The field delimiter for reading/writing CSV data. Must be a single character. If not set, QSV_DEFAULT_DELIMITER is used, else ','. A .tsv/.tab (tab) or .ssv (semicolon) extension on the input or --output file sets that file's delimiter. (default: ,)
Start a new window at this interval. Required in window mode.

Also emit the empty windows between each group's first and last window: count, sum and len are 0 there, and every other aggregation is empty. Window mode only. Requires the default left labels, and cannot be combined with --start-by datapoint or --boundaries.

Read CSV values that can't be parsed as their column's type as empty (null) instead of failing. Their rows are kept. This does not relax the index: its values must still parse as dates (or integers), with none empty.
The date, datetime or integer column that defines the windows. Required. The output keeps its name.
Number of rows to scan when inferring the schema. Set to 0 to scan the entire file.
The value written to the index column for each window. Window mode only. One of: left      - the window's start (the default) right     - the window's end datapoint - the window's first index value
Shift the window boundaries by this duration. Defaults to 0 in window mode, and to minus --period in rolling mode (a look-back window).
Write output to <file> instead of stdout.
The length of each window. Defaults to --every in window mode. Required in rolling mode.
The input is already sorted by --index, within each group when using --by, so skip timebucketp's sort. Unsorted input is then an error, never a wrong result.

Where the first window starts. Window mode only. One of: window    - the --every boundary at or before the first index value (the default) datapoint - the first index value itself monday ... sunday - that weekday (weekly --every)

examples.description: 1-hour windows starting every 15 minutes, computed per station
examples.command: qsv timebucketp -i ts --every 15m --period 1h --by station --agg mean:temp,max:temp readings.csv
